item.name: 401 - Root Path (no route defined, denyAll catchall)

exec: // SecurityConfig's catchall changed from permitAll() to denyAll() -- a
// production review correctly flagged permitAll() as a real security gap
// just harmless unmapped paths). With denyAll(), an unmatched route is now
// rejected by Security before it ever reaches the point where
// NoResourceFoundException would produce a 404. The status is 401, not 403:
// this request carries no credential at all, so Spring Security's
// ExceptionTranslationFilter treats the anonymous principal as needing to
// for the full reasoning and the case (a real-but-insufficient credential)
pm.test('status is 401 (denyAll catchall, anonymous caller)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(401));

request.description: Unmatched routes are now rejected by SecurityConfig's denyAll() catchall before reaching NoResourceFoundException's 404 handling -- see GlobalExceptionHandlerTest for that handler's own coverage, still exercised for authenticated requests to unmapped API sub-paths.

item.name: 429 - Rate Limit (self-contained burst, no Runner iterations needed)

exec: // Self-contained: does NOT depend on Collection Runner 'Iterations'.
// A prior version relied on selecting just this request and setting
// Iterations manually -- easy to get wrong, and running the WHOLE
// collection with N iterations instead re-registers a fresh tenant
// every iteration (Setup > Register Tenant), permanently resetting the
// bucket each time so 429 could never be observed regardless of N.
// This version fires a burst against the SAME, already-registered
// {{apiKey}} entirely within this one script execution via
// pm.sendRequest, chained recursively. Works whether this runs as the
// last step of a full sequential collection pass (bucket already has
// ~19 prior uses from earlier folders -- the burst crosses 20 almost
// immediately) or in isolation right after Setup (bucket starts at 0 --
// the burst crosses 20 partway through 30 calls either way).
